summary: Checkpoint 1 of the R24.3 part (Claude Code cc-39fac3). No integrated decomposition exists; RS-06 and RS-08 keep these stages and route their consumers (ClassicalSerreModularity R26–R33, SmallRamification R25.5). 22 nodes. R24.3: Böckle's presentation, his Lemma 2 (finite plus no more relations than variables gives a finite flat complete intersection) and Theorem 1, KW Annals Theorem 3.3, the lift types of KW I Theorem 5.1 (definition with API and tests) and its four constructions from KW II §10.3.1, the application table, and Snowden's prescribed-type lifts for the modern route. R24.4: KW I Theorem 4.1 from KW II §10.2. R24.5: the Brauer system through a potentially modular lift, its almost strict compatibility, KW I Theorem 5.1 and Dieulefait's families. R24.5:operations: compatible systems with separate strict/almost strict/plain predicates, and twist, restriction, induction. R24.6: residual members, what almost strictness gives at the coefficient prime, and linked systems. Finiteness (R24.1) and points (R24.2) belong to part R23.1. One source issue (a page range in KW II's bibliography).

nodes.title: Böckle's presentation of a global deformation ring (Proposition 1 of the appendix)
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(k) be odd and absolutely irreducible, X a set of local deformation conditions, unramified outside a finite set S, and d ∈ {0, 1}, Ad_X = Ad⁰ρ̄ if X fixes the determinant (d = 0) and Ad_X = Adρ̄ otherwise (d = 1). Suppose (a) for ℓ ∈ S ∖ {p, ∞} the local ring R_{X,ℓ} is a complete intersection, flat over ℤ_p, of relative dimension h⁰(G_ℓ, Ad_X) − Δ_ℓ, and (b) R_{X,p} is a complete intersection, flat over ℤ_p, of relative dimension h⁰(G_p, Ad_X) + 1 + d − Δ_p. Then with Δ = ΣΔ_ℓ, R_X ≅ 𝒪⟦x₁, …, x_{n+d}⟧/(f₁, …, f_{n+Δ}) for some n. In particular, when Δ ≤ 0 (for instance minimal conditions, where Δ_ℓ = 0) the ring has at most as many relations as variables (Böckle's Corollary 1; KW Annals Proposition 3.4: W⟦X₁, …, X_r⟧/(f₁, …, f_s) with r ≥ s).
hypotheses: oddness of ρ̄ enters through the global Euler characteristic (Böckle's formula [1, Lemma 5.5(ii)])
the local hypotheses are hypotheses: they are supplied by LocalGaloisDeformationRings (R08.6), not proved here
this is a presentation, not a lift-existence theorem: finiteness over 𝒪 must be added (R24.1)
proofSteps: Choose auxiliary primes S_aux (Böckle [1], Corollary 6.4) and local presentations R_{X,ℓ} = 𝒪⟦X_{ℓ,1}, …⟧/J_ℓ.
Böckle [1], Theorem 5.6: R_X ≅ 𝒪⟦x₁, …, x_{n+d}⟧/J with J generated by at most Σ j_ℓ elements.
Count n + d from the tangent space with the global Euler characteristic (oddness) to get n + Δ = Σ j_ℓ.
acceptance: Check the count on the minimal case: every Δ_ℓ = 0, so the number of relations is at most the number of variables
Check the sign convention for d and Ad_X against GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.3's presentation

nodes.title: Finite plus few relations gives a finite flat complete intersection (Böckle's Lemma 2)
nodes.statement: Let 𝒪 be a discrete valuation ring and R a complete noetherian local 𝒪-algebra, finitely generated as an 𝒪-module, with a presentation R ≅ 𝒪⟦x₁, …, x_n⟧/(f₁, …, f_m) with m ≤ n. Then m = n, (π, f₁, …, f_n) is a regular sequence, and R is a complete intersection, finite and flat over 𝒪; in particular R[1/π] ≠ 0, so R has a point over the integers of a finite extension of Frac 𝒪.
hypotheses: finiteness over 𝒪 is essential: 𝒪⟦x⟧/(0) has m = 0 ≤ n = 1 but is not finite, and is not a complete intersection of dimension 1 over 𝒪 in the required sense
this is the commutative-algebra core of "finiteness plus presentation gives lifts"; KW II use the same principle in the form of their Corollary 4.7 (R24.2)
proofSteps: A = 𝒪⟦x₁, …, x_n⟧ is regular local of dimension n + 1; R/(π) is finite over k, so I = (π, f₁, …, f_m) has height n + 1, which forces m = n.
In a regular local ring a system of parameters is a regular sequence, so (π, f₁, …, f_n) is regular: R is a complete intersection and π is a nonzerodivisor on R, i.e. R is flat over 𝒪.
acceptance: Check the height count on n = 1: 𝒪⟦x⟧/(x² − π) is finite free of rank 2 over 𝒪
Check that m < n is impossible for finite R (the Krull height argument)

nodes.statement: In the setting of Khare's Inventiones 154 (2003) paper, suppose that for some auxiliary set of primes Q the map R_Q → T_Q is an isomorphism of finite flat W(k)-algebras. Then the canonical map R_∅ → T_∅ of minimal rings is an isomorphism. nodes.title: Minimally ramified lifts (Khare–Wintenberger, Annals, Theorem 3.3)
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) be of S-type with p > 2, ρ̄|_{ℚ(µ_p)} absolutely irreducible, 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 and k(ρ̄) ≠ p. Then ρ̄ has a lift that is minimally ramified at every prime; when k(ρ̄) = p + 1 it may be chosen of crystalline type (Hodge–Tate weights (0, p)) or of semistable type (weight 2). Proof: the minimal deformation ring R^univ has a presentation with r ≥ s (Böckle, Proposition 3.4), is finite over W (Proposition 3.8: Lemma 3.6 reduces finiteness to finiteness of the universal mod-p image, which follows from Taylor's potential modularity and Fujiwara's R = T over a totally real F), hence is finite flat and a complete intersection (Theorem 3.7), so it has a point in characteristic zero. This is the method suggested in the Remark in §5.2 of Khare's Inventiones 154 (2003) paper, which the later KW II Theorem 5.1 generalises.
hypotheses: k(ρ̄) ≠ p: the local ring at p in that weight is not covered by the Fontaine–Laffaille and Ramakrishna/Taylor inputs used here
at k(ρ̄) = p + 1 the crystalline local ring R_{p,crys} is formally smooth of dimension 1 (Böckle; KW Annals Proposition 3.5)
the rationality of the lifts is not controlled
proofSteps: Local rings: flat complete intersections of the right dimension (Ramakrishna, Taylor; R_{p,crys} by Proposition 3.5).
Proposition 3.4 (R24.3/bockle-presentation) and Lemma 3.6 (finiteness criterion).
Proposition 3.8: finiteness via potential modularity (R23) and R = T over F (R22).

nodes.title: Lifts of required type (KW I Theorem 5.1 (1)–(4))
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) be of S-type with 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 if p > 2, non-solvable image if p = 2, and ρ̄|_{ℚ(µ_p)} absolutely irreducible if p > 2. A lift ρ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝒪′) of ρ̄ is of required type (i) if: (1) (k(ρ̄) = 2 when p = 2) ρ is minimally ramified at every ℓ ≠ p and crystalline of weight k(ρ̄) at p; (2) ρ has weight 2, is minimally ramified at ℓ ≠ p, and its inertial Weil–Deligne parameter at p is (ω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2} ⊕ 1, 0), or (id, N) with N ≠ 0 nilpotent when k(ρ̄) = p + 1 (k(ρ̄) = 4 if p = 2); (3) for an odd q ∥ N(ρ̄) with p | q − 1, ρ̄|_{I_q} = (χ ∗; 0 1): ρ is as in (2) at p and minimal at ℓ ≠ p, q, and ρ|_{I_q} ≅ (χ′ ∗; 0 1) for a character χ′ = ω_q^i (0 < i ≤ q − 2) lifting χ, with i even if p = 2; (4) for q ≠ p with ρ̄|_{D_q} ≅ (χ_p ∗; 0 1) up to unramified twist and p | q + 1: ρ is as in (2) at p and minimal at ℓ ≠ p, q, and ρ|_{I_q} ≅ χ′ ⊕ χ′^q for a level-2 character χ′ = ω_{q,2}^iω_{q,2}^{qj} of p-power order, with i + j even if p = 2. "Minimal" is in the sense of Diamond §3 (KW II §3.3.1 at p = 2). Lifts of required type are the 𝒪′-points of R̄^ψ_S for the corresponding local conditions (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.6).

nodes.title: Weight-two lifts with prescribed types (Snowden Theorem 7.2.1; Gee)
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real and ρ̄ : G_F → GL₂(𝔽̄_p) odd with (A1) ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible and (A2) if p = 5 and the projective image is PGL₂(𝔽₅) then [F(ζ₅) : F] = 4. For a lifting problem P = (Σ, ψ, t, {τ_v}) — Σ containing the ramified places and those above p, ψ of finite order with det ρ̄ = ψ̄χ̄_p, a definite type t(v) and an inertial type τ_v at each v ∈ Σ — there are finitely many solutions (weight-two lifts with these data), and a solution exists iff a local solution exists (Theorem 7.2.1). If t is a definite type function on Σ′ ⊆ Σ compatible with ρ̄, then ρ̄ has a weight-two lift unramified outside Σ with determinant ψχ_p and type t on Σ′ (Theorem 7.6.1). Over F = ℚ, (A2) is automatic, and this gives Dieulefait–Pacetti Theorem 1.9(4) (crystalline at p if k(ρ̄) = 2, Steinberg if k(ρ̄) = p + 1). It is used only by the modern route.

nodes.title: Compatible systems: strict, almost strict, and plain
nodes.statement: For a number field E and number field F, an E-rational two-dimensional strictly compatible system (ρ_ι) of G_F consists of: for each prime ℓ and embedding ι : E ↪ ℚ̄_ℓ, a continuous semisimple geometric ρ_ι : G_F → GL₂(ℚ̄_ℓ); for each prime 𝔮 of F a Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation r_𝔮 with values in GL₂(E), unramified for almost all 𝔮, such that for every ℓ and ι the Weil–Deligne parameter of ρ_ι|_{D_𝔮} is conjugate to r_𝔮 (for 𝔮 above ℓ too, via Fontaine); and integers a ≥ b with Hodge–Tate weights (a, b). It is regular if a ≠ b. It is almost strictly compatible if (ii) b) is only required for 𝔮 not above ℓ and, for 𝔮 above ℓ: when ρ̄_ι is irreducible, ρ_ι is geometric of weights (a, b) with (ii) b); and when ℓ ≠ 2 and r_𝔮 is unramified, ρ_ι|_{D_𝔮} is crystalline of weights (a, b). It is compatible if the ρ_ι are only continuous, semisimple and finitely ramified, with (ii) b) away from ℓ and crystalline of weights (a, b) at 𝔮 | ℓ for ℓ ≫ 0. Dieulefait–Pacetti's Definition 1.10 is the same notion as a 5-tuple (K, S, {Q_ℓ(x)}, {ρ_𝔭}, k).
hypotheses: the local predicates (strict, almost strict, plain) are kept separate; almost strictness gives no Weil–Deligne information at 𝔮 | ℓ when ρ̄_ι is reducible and r_𝔮 is ramified

nodes.title: Twisting, restriction and induction of compatible systems
nodes.statement: Let (ρ_ι) be an E-rational compatible system of G_F of rank n (strict, almost strict or plain). (i) For an E-rational system of characters (χ_ι) (for instance the ℓ-adic incarnations of a Hecke character of type A₀), (ρ_ι ⊗ χ_ι) is a system of the same kind, with r_𝔮 ⊗ χ_𝔮. (ii) For F′/F finite, (ρ_ι|_{G_{F′}}) is a system of the same kind with the restricted Weil–Deligne data. (iii) For F/F₀ finite, (Ind_{G_F}^{G_{F₀}} ρ_ι) is a system of rank n[F : F₀] with the induced Weil–Deligne data. (iv) Virtual combinations Σ n_i Ind(χ_i ⊗ ρ_i) have well-defined traces at almost all Frobenius elements; whether they are true representations is a separate statement (R24.5/brauer-induction-system). Irreducibility, regularity and purity are NOT preserved automatically: restriction can make a system reducible, and induction changes the Hodge–Tate multiset.

nodes.statement: Let (ρ_ι) be an E-rational almost strictly compatible, irreducible, odd two-dimensional system of G_ℚ with weights (a, b), and ρ̄_ι the semisimplified reductions. (i) det ρ̄_ι is the reduction of det ρ_ι, and ρ̄_ι is odd. (ii) ρ̄_ι is absolutely irreducible for almost all ι (bounded conductor, fixed Hodge–Tate weights). (iii) For q ≠ ℓ, the Artin conductor of ρ̄_ι at q divides that of r_q, so N(ρ̄_ι) divides the prime-to-ℓ conductor of the system; the prime divisors of N(ρ̄_ι) are among the ramified primes of the system other than ℓ. (iv) If ρ(I_q) is finite of order prime to ℓ (for instance a dihedral group of order 2t^a with t ≠ ℓ), reduction is injective on it, so ρ̄_ι|_{I_q} has the same shape. (v) If ℓ is outside the ramification set, ℓ ≠ 2 and a − b + 1 ≤ ℓ − 1, then ρ_ι is crystalline at ℓ and k(ρ̄_ι) = a − b + 1 up to twist (Fontaine–Laffaille).

nodes.title: Linked systems and modularity transfer
nodes.statement: (i) A compatible system is modular if and only if one of its members is (Dieulefait–Pacetti Remark 4): if ρ_λ ≅ ρ_{f,λ} for a newform f, the strictly compatible system of f has the same Frobenius traces at almost all primes as every member, so each member is ρ_{f,ι} by Brauer–Nesbitt (and Chebotarev). (ii) Two systems (ρ_ι), (ρ′_ι) are linked at λ if ρ̄_λ ≅ ρ̄′_λ. If (ρ′_ι) is modular and ρ_λ satisfies the hypotheses of a modularity lifting theorem with residual input ρ̄_λ (KW I Theorem 4.1, R24.4; or the modern theorems of GL2ModularityLifting R32.6), then (ρ_ι) is modular. This is how modularity moves along the chains of KW I §§8–9 and of the modern route.

sources.locator: Remark 4, p. 7 of the arXiv version
sources.excerpt: If ρ is part of a compatible system of Galois representations {ρp}, then ρ is modular if and only if any given member of the family is.

requests.need: Snowden's local deformation rings of definite type (Propositions 7.3.1 and 7.4.1 of arXiv:0905.4266): nonzero, of the right dimension, for every definite type compatible with ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}}, including v | p (weight two), with the existence of a definite-type lift of the same conductor (Proposition 7.7.1).

The weight part of Serre's conjecture for modular ρ̄ as KW II §10.2 uses it: ρ̄ arises from S_{k(ρ̄)}(Γ₁(N)) with p ∤ N and from S₂(Γ₁(Np)) (Gross, Theorem 13.10 and Propositions 8.13, 8.18; Coleman–Voloch).

Serre weights of residual representations for the weight bookkeeping of KW I Theorem 5.1(3),(4), with Savitt's computation of the reductions of potentially Barsotti–Tate representations of tame type (Duke 128 (2005), Corollary 6.15 and Remark 6.17).
The definitions of S-type, k(ρ̄), N(ρ̄) and "modular" used in KW I Theorems 4.1 and 5.1.
Langlands' solvable base change and descent for Hilbert modular forms, as used in KW II §§9–10 (descent of modularity along allowable base changes; the π_i of the Brauer argument).
Weil–Deligne parameters of ℓ-adic representations and their compatibility with twist, restriction and induction.
Artin conductors and their behaviour under reduction.
Residual images: absolute irreducibility and oddness of residual members.
Recognition of semisimple representations by Frobenius polynomials (Brauer–Nesbitt with Chebotarev).

coverage.notes: Böckle's presentation, Lemma 2 and Theorem 1 (the pinned earlier input) with KW Annals Theorem 3.3; the lift types of KW I Theorem 5.1 and its four constructions from KW II §10.3.1 (finiteness R24.1, dimension from GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.3, points R24.2, local nonemptiness from LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6); the application table; Snowden's prescribed-type lifts for the modern route.
KW I Theorem 4.1 from KW II §10.2: the residual inputs (α), (β) from modularity, then Theorem 9.7 (GL2ModularityLifting R22.5/R22.6) after an allowable base change and descent.

KW II §10.3.2: the Brauer system through a potentially modular lift, its almost strict compatibility (with the authors' withdrawal of strictness), KW I Theorem 5.1 with the residual weights (Savitt requested), and Dieulefait's families in the form of DP Theorem 1.11.

remaining: Rank-n and polarised systems with tensor products, duals and symmetric and exterior powers (RS-12 is not yet accepted; the operations layer is planned only as far as rank 2 needs).
coverage.notes: The definition of compatible systems with the strict, almost strict and plain predicates kept separate, and twisting, restriction and induction.

Residual members (determinant, oddness, irreducibility for almost all ι, conductor, inertia, weight), what almost strictness gives at the coefficient prime (including the de Rham-only case used by the modern route), and linked systems.
